knowledge:
- key_parameters: workingDir=The physical directory on disk where the workspace cache and outputs are stored ;; maxThreadNumber=The maximum number of threads to use for parallel processing ;; sample=A sample handle object created by selex.sample representing a specific sequencing run and round ;; order=The order of the Markov model to build (set to NA to automatically evaluate multiple orders) ;; crossValidationSample=The sample handle used as a testing dataset for cross-validating the Markov model ;; Kmax=The maximum oligonucleotide length for cross-validation, typically found using selex.kmax ;; k=The oligonucleotide length (motif length) for which counts or affinities are calculated ;; markovModel=The Markov model object built using selex.mm used to compute expected background frequencies
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have SELEX-seq data (including initial round 0 and selected rounds) and want to build background Markov models of the initial pool, identify the optimal transcription factor binding site length, and calculate relative binding affinities and standard errors for all K-mers of that length.
- pitfalls: You must set the maximum Java memory limit using options(java.parameters="-Xmx1500M") before loading the SELEX library, otherwise rJava may run out of memory. You must also make samples visible to the session using selex.loadAnnotation or selex.defineSample before attempting to create sample handles with selex.sample.

workflows.name: selex_seq_analysis
workflows.intent: Quantify DNA binding specificities and estimate K-mer affinities from SELEX-seq data.
input: sample_annotation.xml (XML database containing sample metadata like round, barcode, variable region, and file paths)
R0.fastq.gz (FASTQ file for the initial round 0 pool)
R2.fastq.gz (FASTQ file for the selected round 2 pool)
workflows.stages: 1. Configure workspace and set Java memory options ;; 2. Load sample annotations and define sample handles for training, testing, and selected rounds ;; 3. Determine the maximum K-mer length (Kmax) for cross-validation ;; 4. Build and evaluate Markov models of the initial pool to select the optimal order ;; 5. Calculate information gain across different oligonucleotide lengths to find the optimal motif length ;; 6. Generate K-mer count tables and estimate relative affinities and standard errors
workflows.code:
options(java.parameters="-Xmx1500M")
library(SELEX) 
workDir = "./cache/"
selex.config(workingDir=workDir, maxThreadNumber=4)
exampleFiles = selex.exampledata(workDir)
selex.loadAnnotation(exampleFiles[3])
selex.sampleSummary()
r0train = selex.sample(seqName="R0.libraries", 
            sampleName="R0.barcodeGC", round=0)
r0test = selex.sample(seqName="R0.libraries", 
           sampleName="R0.barcodeCG", round=0)
r2 = selex.sample(seqName="R2.libraries", 
       sampleName="ExdHox.R2", round=2)
kmax.value = selex.kmax(sample=r0test)
mm = selex.mm(sample=r0train, order=NA, 
       crossValidationSample=r0test, Kmax=kmax.value)
selex.mmSummary()
selex.infogain(sample=r2,markovModel=mm)
selex.infogainSummary()[,1:3]
infoscores = selex.infogainSummary()
idx = which(infoscores$InformationGain==max(infoscores$InformationGain))
optimalLength = infoscores$K[idx]
table = selex.counts(sample=r2, k=optimalLength, 
          markovModel=mm)
head(table)
aff = selex.affinities(sample=r2, k=optimalLength, 
        markovModel=mm)
head(aff)[,1:4]
head(aff)[,5:6]
